name: HUP – Sincroniza productos en planillas
author: HazmeUnaPagina.cl

sections.description:
HUP – Sincroniza productos en planillas imports and exports existing simple WooCommerce products through a Google Sheets spreadsheet in your own Google account. It supports manually selected directions, scheduled runs and an optional Google Apps Script button. The plugin uses your own Google Cloud OAuth credentials.

This is an independent plugin by HazmeUnaPagina.cl. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by WooCommerce, Automattic or Google. WooCommerce and Google Sheets are trademarks of their respective owners.

The admin interface is in Spanish. WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Supported in this free plugin:

  • Existing simple products, including virtual and downloadable simple products for their common fields. It does not change virtual or download settings.
  • Product name, slug, description, categories, tags, brand when the taxonomy exists, regular price, sale price, SKU, and stock when managed by WooCommerce.
  • Selected and ordered spreadsheet columns and explicitly configured scalar custom metadata.
  • Product ID, type and publication status as reference data. Import updates existing products by WooCommerce ID; it does not create products or change their type.
  • No product-count, run-count or time limit imposed by this plugin. Hosting and Google API limits still apply.

Variable products, variations, external and grouped products, and third-party product types are outside this plugin’s synchronization scope. A separately distributed Pro add-on is planned to support existing variable products and variations. Neither version’s initial scope includes creating products or editing downloadable files and settings.

Each manual, scheduled or webhook run operates in one selected direction. Review the synchronization history for skipped rows and errors. Use a dedicated spreadsheet and keep a backup before your first export.

External service: Google

This plugin relies on Google OAuth and the Google Sheets API. It cannot connect to or synchronize a spreadsheet without a Google account, a Google Cloud project with the Sheets API enabled, and OAuth web application credentials supplied by the site administrator. It does not transmit product data to HUP servers.

When an administrator connects a Google account, the browser visits accounts.google.com and the site exchanges the authorization code with oauth2.googleapis.com. The site also calls www.googleapis.com to read the connected account’s email address. Access tokens can be refreshed via oauth2.googleapis.com; disconnecting may call Google’s token revocation endpoint. The requested Google Sheets OAuth scope allows the app to see, edit, create and delete all Google Sheets spreadsheets in the connected account, although the plugin works with the configured spreadsheet. Google classifies this scope as sensitive. The plugin also requests email access to identify the connected account.

When an administrator creates a spreadsheet, starts an import or export, enables a scheduled synchronization, or invokes the optional Apps Script webhook, the site calls sheets.googleapis.com. For exports, Google receives the enabled product columns, which can include IDs, names, descriptions, categories, tags, brand, prices, SKU, stock and custom metadata selected by the administrator. Imports read those spreadsheet values from Google into the WooCommerce site. The optional Apps Script sends the selected direction and a site webhook token to the site’s REST endpoint; keep this token private.

OAuth client credentials, access and refresh tokens, the connected email and plugin settings are stored in the site’s WordPress database. Administrators should select only metadata suitable for storage in their Google spreadsheet, and consider their own privacy policy for any personal data they choose to export.

  • Google Privacy Policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate this plugin, then open “HUP Sincronización” in the admin menu.
  3. In Google Cloud Console, enable the Google Sheets API and configure the OAuth consent screen with the External user type.
  4. Publish the app: in Google Auth Platform > Audience, click Publish app so the publishing status is In production. While the app is in Testing mode, Google blocks the connection with 403 access_denied and expires it after 7 days. Verification is not required; when connecting, Google shows “Google hasn’t verified this app”: choose Advanced > Go to (your app).
  5. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials for a web application. Add the exact redirect URI displayed on the plugin’s Guide tab.
    For a Local test site using a .local domain, switch Local’s Router Mode to localhost first, apply its Fix It prompt if shown, and copy the updated redirect URI. Google does not accept .local redirect domains.
  6. Enter the client ID and secret on the Connection tab and authorize your Google account.
  7. Create a spreadsheet or enter its ID and sheet name, choose columns, then run an export or import.
sections.faq:
Does the free plugin stop after 50 products?

No. It has no plugin-imposed product limit. It synchronizes supported simple products regardless of the store’s total product count, subject to hosting and Google API limits.

Can I create products by adding spreadsheet rows?

No. Import updates existing simple products identified by their WooCommerce IDs.

Are virtual or downloadable simple products supported?

Their common product fields are supported. The virtual setting, downloadable files, download limit and expiry are left unchanged.

How should I write prices in the spreadsheet?

Write the number without a thousands separator, for example 19990. Spreadsheets created by the plugin for Chilean stores use the Chile locale. If you use an existing spreadsheet whose locale has a decimal point, stores without decimals cannot import price changes until you change it in File > Settings, because Google reads 20.000 as 20.

Does this plugin sync variable products?

No. Variable products and their variations are outside the free plugin’s scope. A separate Pro add-on is planned for existing variable products and variations.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Changed: internal prefix unified. Sites using 1.0.0 must enter their Google credentials, connect again, select their columns and paste the new Apps Script.
  • Fixed: prices written with thousands separators (19.990) are rejected instead of being read as decimals.
  • Fixed: partial imports show a readable summary instead of raw JSON, with updated, unchanged, skipped and failed rows.
  • Fixed: trashed products are skipped, and missing columns are reported as warnings instead of errors.
  • Fixed: interrupted synchronizations no longer appear as running, and backslashes in custom metadata are kept.
  • Improved: prices are exported as numbers, and new spreadsheets use the store’s locale.
  • Improved: large synchronizations use fewer queries and finish even if the connection is closed.
  • Improved: the spreadsheet button explains when Google cannot reach the site.
  • Improved: confirmation before exporting and before regenerating the token.

1.0.0

  • Initial release for synchronization of existing simple WooCommerce products with Google Sheets.
